title: QuSecure’s QuProtect R3 PQC Platform Added to Carahsoft’s GSA Schedule Contract - Quantum Computing Report
gist: QuSecure's QuProtect R3 post-quantum cryptography platform has been added to Carahsoft's GSA Schedule (Contract 47QSWA18D008F), clearing the procurement path for U.S. federal defense, intelligence, and civilian agencies facing NSM-10 deadlines of December 31, 2030 for key establishment and December 31, 2031 for digital signatures. The product is positioned as an external cryptographic control plane that swaps algorithms across legacy, cloud, and air-gapped estates without code rewrites, monetized through compliance artifacts like single-click CBOM generation.

themes.theme: Contract-Vehicle Access as the Federal Wedge

insights.claim: QuSecure's QuProtect R3 encryption modernization platform has been added to Carahsoft Technology's GSA Schedule contract (Contract No. 47QSWA18D008F), removing a procurement hurdle for U.S. federal defense, intelligence, and civilian buyers of post-quantum cryptography.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Schedule listing is the gating event before federal PQC revenue can be booked at scale; it marks the transition from pilot sales to catalog purchasing.
insights.quote: The contract addition simplifies procurement for U.S. federal defense, intelligence, and civilian agencies seeking to meet federal post-quantum migration mandates.
insights.locator: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and crypto-agility software provider

insights.claim: Beyond the GSA Schedule, QuSecure's products reach buyers through NASA SEWP V (NNG15SC03B, NNG15SC27B), U.S. Army ITES-SW2 (W52P1J-20-D-0042), NASPO ValuePoint (AR2472), and OMNIA Partners (R240303), spanning federal, defense, and state/local cooperative purchasing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Breadth of contract vehicles is the practical measure of a govtech vendor's addressable pipeline; count vehicles, not press releases, when sizing public-sector security plays.
insights.locator: In addition to the GSA Schedule

insights.claim: A government IT aggregator, Carahsoft, rather than the security vendor itself, controls the distribution layer through which post-quantum cryptography reaches U.S. agencies, making channel placement a determinant of which PQC vendors capture the mandate-driven spend.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Aggregators capture a toll on the entire federal PQC migration regardless of which encryption vendor wins on technical merit.
insights.locator: In addition to the GSA Schedule

themes.theme: NSM-10 Deadlines as a Dated Demand Curve

insights.claim: Executive orders and National Security Memorandum 10 require high-value federal information systems to upgrade key establishment protocols by December 31, 2030 and digital signature algorithms by December 31, 2031, putting hard calendar dates on U.S. government post-quantum migration spending.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: These two dates define a legally mandated, non-discretionary budget cycle for cryptographic modernization vendors through the end of the decade.
insights.quote: upgrade key establishment protocols by December 31, 2030, and digital signature algorithms by December 31, 2031
insights.locator: The addition addresses federal timelines set by executive orders

insights.claim: Federal PQC demand is being pulled forward by compliance mandates rather than by any demonstrated quantum attack, so the buying trigger for this category is regulatory deadline risk, not cryptographically relevant quantum hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: PQC vendor revenue tracks the compliance calendar and audit cycles, which makes it more forecastable and less dependent on quantum hardware milestones than the sector's narrative suggests.
insights.locator: The addition addresses federal timelines set by executive orders

insights.claim: QuProtect R3 sits as an external cryptographic control plane that lets administrators swap encryption algorithms and enforce crypto-agility policy across legacy, cloud, and air-gapped environments without altering application source code or running infrastructure rip-and-replace cycles.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An overlay that avoids code rewrites is the only migration model that fits 2030 deadlines on legacy federal estates, which favors control-plane vendors over library-level or hardware replacement approaches.
insights.quote: without altering underlying application source code or triggering infrastructure “rip-and-replace” cycles
insights.locator: Operating as an external cryptographic control plane

insights.claim: The platform packages PQC migration as three continuous functions rather than a one-time upgrade: live packet inspection and cryptographic asset discovery, downtime-free algorithm swapping, and automated audit telemetry.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Recurring discovery-and-governance framing converts a finite migration project into a subscription surface, which is the difference between one-time and annuity revenue in this category.
insights.quote: Enables dynamic algorithm swapping and crypto-agile policy updates without system downtime or code refactoring.

insights.claim: Single-click Cryptographic Bill of Materials generation aligned to NSA CNSA 2.0, CNSSP 15, FIPS, and GDPR is the platform's compliance hook, making the auditable artifact rather than the encryption itself the deliverable agencies buy.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: CBOM output is becoming the standard procurement checkbox for cryptographic modernization, so watch it as the emerging requirement that filters vendor shortlists.
insights.quote: generates single-click Cryptographic Bill of Materials (CBOM) outputs aligned with NSA CNSA 2.0, CNSSP 15, FIPS, and GDPR standards

insights.claim: Coverage explicitly extends to air-gapped and on-premises legacy networks, not just TLS and cloud traffic, which is where classified and defense workloads that cannot be re-architected actually sit.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Air-gap capability is the qualifier for intelligence and defense deals, a segment cloud-native security vendors structurally cannot serve.
